question: I recently read in a security blog: "CERT-UA says PurpleFox typically infects systems when victims launch laced MSI installers and highlights its self-propagation capabilities using exploits for known flaws and password brute-forcing." Can you identify the MITRE ATT&CK category for this behavior and explain how it maps to that technique? Also, how can we detect this behavior in our SOC using logs, sensors, or NDR tools according to the x_mitre_detection guidance?
answer: 1) MITRE ATT&CK Category: T1218.007 - Msiexec. 2) Mapping Explanation: The behavior of infecting systems via laced MSI installers maps to the Msiexec technique because it involves the execution of malicious MSI files, a process which attackers leverage to initiate further propagation and exploit system flaws. 3) Detection Methods: According to x_mitre_detection, detection can be achieved by monitoring the execution and arguments of msiexec.exe. This involves comparing the current invocations and arguments against a history of known good executions and scrutinizing any associated command-line arguments before and after msiexec.exe runs to identify potentially adversarial activities.
